findings.title: Table widget feature flag renders an empty table instead of the actual data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the org has `use-table-widget-visualization` the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. All of the already-fetched `result.data`/`result.meta`/`eventView`/custom renderers are ignored, so any org with this flag enabled gets a completely blank table (and no loading placeholder either, since `loading` is no longer passed). This is a user-visible regression gated only by a feature flag rather than a WIP placeholder, so it will break dashboards as soon as the flag is turned on. The branch should pass through the real `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns` (and handle `loading`), or not be wired up yet.

findings.title: useTraceItemAttributeKeys can now return undefined attributes instead of an empty TagCollection
findings.body: The hook was rewritten to `useQuery` and returns `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data`. Before this change `attributes` was always an object (a `TagCollection` built from `result.data ?? []`, defaulting to `{}`). Now, while the query is disabled (`enabled: false`), before the first fetch resolves (`data` is `undefined` and `previous` is `undefined`), or if the query is skipped, `attributes` is `undefined`. Callers that treat the result as a `TagCollection` (e.g. iterating it, spreading/merging it into a tag map, or calling `Object.keys`/`hasOwnProperty`) will throw. Either default `data` (`data ?? {}`) or keep the empty-object fallback.

findings.title: Error details are paired with event IDs by list position, which can misattribute errors
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())` where `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`. This assumes the returned dict contains exactly one entry per requested id, in the same order as `error_ids`. If the nodestore backend omits ids it couldn't find (common for `get_multi` implementations), all pairs after the first missing id shift, so an error's title/message is attached to the wrong event id. Even if the backend returns a `None` value for misses, the code still relies on dict iteration order matching `error_ids`. Build the result from `events.items()` (recovering the event id from the key/node_id) or map event ids to data explicitly.
